desc: Ideation: model game as bipartite components with bipartitions (a_i,b_i); total moves T = A*B - M where (A,B) is the final merged bipartition; N odd ⇒ T parity fixed (= M mod 2, Aoki iff M odd); N even ⇒ players influence A parity via merge orientations ("decisive merges" involve odd-sized components; last decisive merger sets A parity, subject to empty-side restrictions for isolated vertices).
Brute-force tiny cases (N≤6) with memoized game search to get ground-truth winners; generate many random bipartite graphs. (script written, samples 1-2 verified)
Theoretical analysis: N-odd rule proved (Aoki ⟺ M odd); k=0 proved (Aoki ⟺ (base+M) odd); k=2 with ≤1 singleton proved (Aoki wins); open cells: k=2 both singletons C≥3, and k≥4 timing game.

Derive the k≥4 and k=2-two-singletons rule via the abstract timing game (passes = fills + even-even merges; odd+odd merges reduce k by 2; the k:2→0 merger wins), update fast_winner, and verify with the harness (exhaustive N≤5, random N=6,7) until zero mismatches.
Implement final O(N+M) solution: iterative BFS/DSU 2-coloring for (a_i,b_i) per component, compute N%2, M%2, k, base, singles, P, C, apply the verified rule, print Aoki/Takahashi.

Validate final implementation against brute force on exhaustive small cases (N≤5) and ~10^4 random instances (N=6,7); check samples 1-3 and edge cases (N=1, M=0, N=2 two singletons, isolated vertices, single complete bipartite component).
